accounting_warning: This is the first national-balance reconstruction, but not yet a promoted exact inventory. Physical-location bands are stronger than model-by-model totals. Paper divisional organization never overrides traced physical theater location.

large_formations: 1st Tank Division formed 1942 in Manchuria from 1st Tank Group; four-regiment square organization in 1942.
2nd Tank Division formed 1942 in Manchuria; four-regiment square organization in 1942.
3rd Tank Division physical Branch core uses 12th/13th/17th Tank Regiments; 8th Tank Regiment is treated as South-Pacific detached because Branch/1942 theater OOB places it outside China.
23rd/24th Tank Regiments form the Armored Operational Training Brigade in Manchuria.
15th/16th Tank Regiments remain independent Kwantung formations.
source_basis.regimental_scale: 1940-43 tank regiments varied materially. Use 55-75 physical tanks as a practical 1942 field band, rather than multiplying a single paper TOE blindly.
source_basis.production: Use Branch 1935-42 production/retrofit ledgers as inflow. Old Type94/Type89 retirement and repair classes remain banded.

Type95_HaGo_and_tiny_KeNi.note: From >2,000 cumulative Type95 production by end-1942, less combat loss, noncombat writeoff, long repair, training/static conversion.

model_mix_center.47mm_Shinhoto: about 550-650 physical including converted old hulls

Type97_medium_family_all_hulls.important: Shinhoto conversion changes model mix, not physical hull count.

Type89_medium.role: front-line only in selected old regiments/garrisons; increasing training/static/secondary use

Type94_and_Type97_tankettes.role: reconnaissance, divisional tankette companies, security, training; many old Type94s are no longer first-line combat assets

SPG_and_new_small_series.content: Ho-Ni I and tiny experimental/new light-series vehicles

1st_Tank_Division_Manchuria.note: Includes returned/reassigned regimental lineages; do not also count those campaign survivors as separate free pools.

Armored_Operational_Training_Brigade_23r.availability: training/proving reserve, not instantly deployable as two free combat regiments

other_Branch_Pacific_packets.guard: No tank company is spawned at Port Moresby/Santo/Lunga without a dated unit trace.

China_and_other_infantry_recon_security.mostly: Type94/Type97 tankettes, light tanks, armored cars and small attached companies

Home_training_depot_replacement.note: Includes modern replacement tanks plus many older/training vehicles; it is not one deployable formation.

obsolete_static_retirement_candidate.content: mainly Type89/Type94 and worn vehicles still physically extant but poor candidates for mobile campaign allocation

systemic_result.main_finding: Branch reliability/recovery preserves dozens of hulls through early campaigns, but the 1942 armored reorganization absorbs most of the gain into better-filled divisions, training/replacement stocks, and southern garrisons. There is no giant free tank reserve.
systemic_result.free_modern_medium_pool_outside_named_fo: roughly 180-320 serviceable-equivalent at year-end, but fragmented among depots/schools/replacement flows and not available without lead time
double_count_prevention: 1st/6th/7th campaign-returning regiment lineages are absorbed into 1st/2nd Tank Division accounting by year-end.
8th Tank Regiment is South-Pacific tied and excluded from 3rd Tank Division/Five-Go.
captured Allied tanks remain separate and consume distinct spares/ammunition.

next_gate: Post 1943 production, Five-Go attrition/repair, GALVANIC -14 Type95, and theater transfers to produce 1943-12-31 national checkpoint.
